body:
Origin of the Uma-Snehrashmi Prize

The Uma-Snehrashmi Prize, also known as the Uma-Snehrashmi Paritoshik, is a Gujarati literary award administered by the Gujarati Sahitya Parishad, Ahmedabad.

It was established in 1963 by the Gujarati poet Jhinabhai R. Desai, popularly known by his literary name Snehrashmi, in memory of his deceased daughter Uma.

The purpose of the prize is to recognise an outstanding Gujarati literary book published within a specified period, ordinarily covering 2 years. It is associated with the literary activities and biennial knowledge sessions of the Gujarati Sahitya Parishad.

First recipient and selected award-winning works

The first Uma-Snehrashmi Prize was awarded to Umashankar Joshi for Mahaprasthan, covering the initial period 1963–1965.

Subsequent awards have recognised different forms of Gujarati literary writing. The following examples are particularly useful for distinguishing literary works and awards.

PeriodRecipientWork
1963–1965Umashankar JoshiMahaprasthan
1966–1967Ravji PatelJhanjha
1968–1969Jayant KhatriKhara Bapor
1974–1975Raghuveer ChaudhariUparvas novel trilogy
1984–1985Chandrakant ShethDhoolmani Paglio
1998–1999Dhruv BhattTatvamasi

A single literary work may receive recognition from more than one institution. For example, Raghuveer Chaudhari's Uparvas trilogy received the Uma-Snehrashmi Prize for the period 1974–1975 and the national Sahitya Akademi Award for 1977.

Recent prize announcement

The Gujarati Sahitya Parishad's notice dated 10 January 2026 invited entries for the Uma-Snehrashmi Prize covering the publication periods 2022–2023 and 2024–2025. The notice specified recognition of outstanding literary books published during these periods.

The notice establishes the publication periods for the prize selection. It is an invitation for entries, not an announcement of the winning authors.

Comparison of the 5 principal literary honours

Gujarati writers may receive recognition from national literary organisations as well as institutions devoted specifically to Gujarati literature and culture. The awarding institution, basis of recognition and designated award year must be kept distinct.

AwardAwarding institutionBasis of recognition
Jnanpith AwardBharatiya JnanpithOutstanding literary contribution from 1982
Sahitya Akademi AwardSahitya Akademi, national institutionOutstanding book in a recognised language
Ranjitram Suvarna ChandrakGujarat Sahitya Sabha, AhmedabadContribution to Gujarati literature and culture
Narmad Suvarna ChandrakNarmad Sahitya Sabha, SuratOutstanding work in a specified category and period
Uma-Snehrashmi PrizeGujarati Sahitya Parishad, AhmedabadOutstanding Gujarati literary book in a specified period

Umashankar Joshi: recognition across different awards

Umashankar Joshi received all 5 literary honours covered in this lesson. His achievements provide an important example of how the same writer can receive different awards for different works or contributions.

  • 1939: Ranjitram Suvarna Chandrak.
  • 1947: Narmad Suvarna Chandrak for Prachina, associated with the 1943–1947 publication period.
  • 1963–1965: Uma-Snehrashmi Prize for Mahaprasthan.
  • 1967: Jnanpith Award for Nishith, shared with Kuvempu.
  • 1973: Sahitya Akademi Award for Kavini Shraddha.

Important distinctions for objective examinations

The Gujarat Sahitya Sabha and the Gujarati Sahitya Parishad are separate institutions, despite their similar names and common association with Ahmedabad. The former presents the Ranjitram Suvarna Chandrak, while the latter administers the Uma-Snehrashmi Prize.

The Narmad Sahitya Sabha is based in Surat and presents the Narmad Suvarna Chandrak. The Jnanpith Award and the Sahitya Akademi Award belong to national literary institutions.

A writer's famous book, an award-winning book and a writer's overall literary contribution are not necessarily interchangeable. For example, Nishith, Prachina, Mahaprasthan and Kavini Shraddha are all works by Umashankar Joshi, but they are associated with different literary awards.

Prelims focus

  • Uma-Snehrashmi Prize: established in 1963 by Snehrashmi.
  • It commemorates Snehrashmi's daughter Uma.
  • Awarding institution: Gujarati Sahitya Parishad, Ahmedabad.
  • First recipient: Umashankar Joshi for Mahaprasthan.
  • Umashankar Joshi received all 5 literary honours covered in this lesson.
  • Trap: Gujarat Sahitya Sabha and Gujarati Sahitya Parishad are different awarding institutions.

[References: Gujarati Sahitya Kosh, Volume 3, Uma-Snehrashmi Paritoshik and Narmad Chandrak, digitised by Ekatra Foundation; Gujarati Sahitya Parishad, official award notice, Parab, 10 January 2026, p. 63, item 3; Gujarati Sahitya Parishad, literary profiles of Umashankar Joshi and Raghuveer Chaudhari; Gujarati Vishwakosh, Ranjitram Suvarna Chandrak; Bharatiya Jnanpith, official laureate register; Sahitya Akademi, official Gujarati Awards register. Consulted 26 November 2026.]
